steps.text: ANSWER THE SUMMONS — Up the King’s Road, north out of the square.
why: THE CASTLE
Vash was told to send you and told nothing else. Whatever it is, it is above a gate guard.

steps.text: RUN WITH THE BOXERS — Take the three on the open card at the Fighting Pits.
why: THE OPEN CARD
Podd, Vek and Sura, in a line in front of the ring. Anybody can put their name down.

steps.text: RUN WITH THE BIKERS — Win all three circuits, or bring Kelm’s bike out of the volcano yourself.
why: THE RUN
Three circuits, or bring Kelm’s bike out of the mountain yourself. They do not mind which.

steps.text: REPORT TO THE THRONE ROOM — Up the King’s Road. Tell him what both sides told you.
why: LOX IS WAITING
You are the only fox on this planet who has heard both sides say it.

steps.text: BEAT MARSHAL EDE — The sparring cage, past the bunks in the barracks.
why: THE CAGE
Past the bunks. Ask him properly and he will take the bout off anybody.

steps.text: CLEAR THE VOLCANO PLAINS — South out of the square. Ferro says the crowd wants a scar it can see.
why: A SCAR THE CROWD CAN SEE
Half the town walks past these things every day. Ferro says that is the point.

steps.text: GET ON THE CARD — Tace keeps the card, at the booth on Pit Road.
why: THE BOOTH
Tace keeps the card, and the card is a book people read.

steps.text: TAKE THE SAND WITH FERRO — Through the gate, east side of the concourse.
why: THE SAND
He has not had to work in a while.

steps.text: ASK HESSA ABOUT THE ZOO — The keeper’s hut, west end of the Zoo Path.
why: THE KEEPER
The cages are open and she did not open them.

steps.text: CLEAR THE RED PLAINS — Three bridges. Something has been crossing them the wrong way.
why: THREE BRIDGES
Something has been crossing them the wrong way, and going east every time.

steps.text: PUT DOWN THE ASHWALKER — The west flat, past the far end of the north road.
why: THE WEST FLAT
Grey, cold, and it came up THROUGH the ground rather than across it.

steps.text: REPORT TO MARSHAL EDE — The war table, top of the barracks.
why: THE WAR TABLE
Ede has been filing what Nix wrote down. He needs to hear it out loud.

steps.text: TAKE LYRA’S LEDGER — She holds the pit, and has held it three seasons.
why: THE LEDGER
Lyra has been saying this for two seasons and writing it down for three.

steps.text: FIND ORN AT THE CAVE MOUTH — Volcano Plains, south end, in the alcove by the cave.
why: THE CAVE MOUTH
Orn is the last fox who saw the inside of the mountain and came back.

steps.text: GET THROUGH THE CAVE — The bridge, the hall, then the span. Do not stop on the span.
why: INSIDE THE MOUNTAIN
The bridge, the hall, then the span. Do not stop on the span.

steps.text: PUT DOWN THE FIRST CINDER — The chamber past the lake. Nobody has ever reached it.
why: PAST THE LAKE
Nobody has ever reached this chamber. That is not the same as nobody having tried.

steps.text: BRING KELM’S BIKE UP — It is in the chamber, where he left it.
why: KELM’S BIKE
Still where he left it, and the tank is not the part that failed him.

steps.text: TAKE THE LEDGER TO LOX — The throne room, top of the Castle Path.
why: THE THRONE ROOM
He has read the ledger once already. He wants to hear the end of it from you.

quests.title: THE THING IN THE THRONE ROOM

steps.text: DRIVE THEM OFF — Three of them, and they are only there half the time.
why: THEY ARE NOT ALWAYS THERE
Hit one while it is solid. While it is not, nothing you do reaches it.

steps.text: PICK UP WHAT THEY DROPPED — One of them left something on the floor of the nave.
why: ON THE FLOOR OF THE NAVE
Something came off one of them on the way out.

steps.text: NINE IN THE TOWN SQUARE — They were waiting for you to come back down the road.
why: YOU ARE NOT ALONE IN THIS ONE
Put three of them down and both doors open. You earned that; let them work.

steps.text: A BIKE FOR THE PLAINS — Lucius is behind the counter at the Bike Shop.
why: THE RUN WILL PUT YOU ON ONE
The cross is past the far bridge. That is not a walk.

steps.text: WEST OF THE RIVER — Past the far bridge. The map says there is something here.
why: THE THING ON THE MAP IS ALREADY GUARDED
The Ashwalker has not left that clearing once. Put it down and see what it was standing on.

steps.text: THE RAMP IS DOWN — On the east side of the hull. It has been down the whole time.
why: THE RAMP IS ON THE EAST SIDE
It has been down the whole time. Walk up it.

steps.text: THE CRYSTAL OF LUXOR — In a crate on the deck, still where they put it.
why: IT IS STILL IN THE CRATE
They never opened it. It is on the deck, a few steps past the old fox.

steps.text: HE WANTED HER, NOT IT — Five of the King's Own, and you are not going to win this.
why: YOU ARE NOT MEANT TO WIN THIS ONE
Stay on your feet. She only needs you to last.

steps.text: THE PAD IN THE SQUARE — Through the walls, down the road, and do not stop.
why: NOTHING CAN TOUCH YOU AND NOTHING WILL HOLD YOU
The walls are not for you just now. The pad is in the middle of the square.

npcs.name: Ottoline
npcs.greeting: Going south? Then you want two of everything.
npcs.bio: Runs the shop on the square. Stocks for the volcano road, which means water first and everything else second.

npcs.name: Garrow
npcs.greeting: Everything here has been in the fire twice. It holds.
npcs.bio: Forges beside a mountain that does the heating for him. Says it is the only sensible place on the planet to keep a forge.

npcs.name: Vesta
npcs.greeting: Sit down. Whatever you have been walking through, sit down.
npcs.bio: Keeps the tavern. Takes bets on the pit and has never once been caught doing it.

npcs.name: Bruno
npcs.greeting: Hands up, chin down. That is the whole of it, and nobody does it.
npcs.bio: Trains anybody who turns up and shouts at all of them equally. Fought in the pit for eleven years and stopped on his own terms.

npcs.name: Sparrow
npcs.greeting: Anything with wheels. Anything without, try the armory.
npcs.bio: Builds and repairs the volcano-track bikes. Has opinions about everybody's tyre pressure.

npcs.name: Lox

lines.text: My lord.
You came in off the plains, so you have already met the planet.
It burns, it shakes, and it is ours. We stay because leaving is also hard.

topics.label: The ledger. And what was at the bottom of it.
replies: Set it down. No — set it down OPEN, at the last page.
Four surveys of a hole in my own mountain, paid for out of a fighter’s purse because the throne would not fund it. That is the first thing in this book and I did not have to read a word to know it.

You went past the bend. You crossed the span. You put down the thing the whole planet has been walking around the edge of for a hundred years, and then you brought a dead fox’s bike up out of it because his partner was still standing at the door.
It burns, it shakes, and it is ours. I have said that in this hall so many times it stopped meaning anything. It means something today.
Take the maul off the back wall. It has been up there since my father and nobody has ever earned it off him. And take the seal — you are Luxor’s, whatever else you are.

topics.label: What will you do about the cave?
replies: Fund the survey. Properly, with the throne’s name on it, and Lyra running it since she is the only one who has been right about it.
And put a post at the mouth. Not to keep foxes out. To make sure the next one who goes in has somebody counting them back.

topics.label: Why does anyone stay on this planet?
replies: You came in off the plains, so you have already met it.
It burns, it shakes, and it is ours. We stay because leaving is also hard.

topics.label: My lord.
replies: Walk safely. It is the only order I give that anybody keeps.

topics.label: Why do you allow the gangs?
replies: Because half of them are family. Mine included — my sister’s boy has been on the Run’s books since he was fourteen and I have never once pretended not to know.
And because they run the sports. The pit fills every night and the circuits fill every weekend, and a town that is watching something is a town that is not asking me questions.
Which is convenient, because I do not want the questions asked. Not this year.

topics.label: Questions about what?
replies: Defences.
That is the whole answer you are getting, and it is more than the council has had.
Something is coming. I do not know when, I do not know how many, and I am not going to stand here and guess in front of somebody who talks to both gangs.

topics.label: Tell me about the crystal.
replies: It sat in this room. On that stand. It has sat there since before my grandfather and it is not there now, and nobody came through a door.

The Pit swear the Run took it on a bike. The Run swear the Pit walked it out under a coat. Both of them are lying about the other and neither of them is lying about themselves, and that is what frightens me.
Get inside both. Then come back and tell me what neither of them would say to a stranger.

npcs.bio: Leader of Luxor. Wears the coat rather than armour and has never been seen out of it. Nobody alive remembers who took the eye, and the two foxes who could have told you are on his own family crest. Tolerates two gangs in his own streets because half of both are family, and says so out loud, which is the part his council cannot forgive.

npcs.name: Marshal Ede

lines.text: Marshal.
Fighting on this planet is mostly about the ground. Learn where it is soft.
The pit teaches you nothing about that. The pit floor is swept.

topics.label: The Ashwalker is down.
replies: Say that again slowly.
Grey. Cold. Came up through the flat rather than across it. West side of the river.
That is the third this season. THIRD. And every one of them was found east of where it came up, walking further east.
Follow that line back far enough and it does not stop at the red plains. It goes under the road, under the town, and it comes out at the volcano.
Go and see the vault sergeant. There is basalt plate on the second rack and you have earned the right to be difficult to kill.

topics.label: What is the barracks actually for?
replies: Holding a road nobody wants and everybody uses.
That is not a complaint. A road nobody wants is exactly the kind that gets taken.

topics.label: Teach me the ground.
replies: I cannot teach you the ground with words. Nobody can. The ground is a thing your feet learn while you are busy being frightened.
The cage is past the bunks. Ask me properly and we will go and find out what your feet know.

topics.label: How do you police two gangs?
replies: I do not. I police the space between them, which is a road and a market and about four hundred foxes who never asked to be there.

The Pit will not use a weapon because they think it is beneath them. The Run will not use a weapon because they are already gone. Between those two kinds of pride the King got a law that mostly works.
Mostly. Ask the trader whose stall went through a window last spring how much comfort mostly is.

topics.label: Could you take the gangs if you had to?
replies: The Pit? Yes, and I would lose foxes doing it, and half the pit is somebody’s cousin in this barracks.
The Run? No. Not with what I have. You cannot arrest a thing that is four streets away before you have finished shouting.
So we do not have to. That is the entire strategy and I will thank you not to test it.

npcs.bio: Runs the barracks off a war table nobody is allowed to lean on.

npcs.name: Ferro

lines.text: You fight in the pit?
When the card is worth it. Most nights it is two hopefuls and a crowd that would cheer a rockfall.
Come and watch a real one. You will learn more in six minutes than a month on the plains.
Any advice for the plains?
The brutes out there swing once and mean it. Make them miss and they have given you the fight.
And do not fight uphill of a vent. It is not the heat, it is the footing.

topics.label: I want a place on the card.
replies: No.
Not no forever. No the way it is currently asked. The pit does not take strangers, it takes foxes the crowd already has an opinion about.
So go and be worth an opinion. Two things do it here, and they are both a walk away.
One: Marshal Ede keeps a sparring cage in the barracks and will take a bout off anybody who asks. Beat him and the barracks talks.
Two: the volcano plains, south of the square, are crawling. Clear them and the ROAD talks, which is louder.
Do both. Then come back and I will not say no.

topics.label: Any advice for the plains?
replies: The brutes out there swing once and mean it. Make them miss and they have given you the fight.
And do not fight uphill of a vent. It is not the heat, it is the footing.

topics.label: Who holds the pit?
replies: Lyra. Three seasons, and she has never once fought like someone protecting a belt.
Every purse she takes goes somewhere. Ask her about it when she decides you are worth answering.

topics.label: I will let you drink.
replies: Left hand. Always the left. Go on.

topics.label: What do you make of the two gangs?
replies: The Pit fight honestly and think that makes them good. The Run do not fight at all and think that makes them clever. Both of them are half right and neither will hear it.
The quarrel is older than the trophies and the trophies are older than me. It has never once put a body in the ground, which is more than my trade can say.

npcs.bio: Luxor's duellist. Fights left-handed, drinks right-handed, and has never explained which one is the lie.

npcs.name: Lyra

lines.text: You are the champion here.
Today. That is all a belt ever means, and anyone who tells you different is selling seats.
Stand at the barrier a while. Watch the feet, not the hands.
What is down in the volcano cave?
Heat, and something that was walking around in it long before we put torches down there.
I go back every season. One of these seasons I will bring an answer out with me.

topics.label: Set up the belt match.
replies: Vek and Sura in the same week. All right.
Ferro does not fight on the open card, he IS the card — and the card is mine. I am putting you on it.
He will be down before you have finished stretching. East side of the concourse, through the gate. Take the barrier side; he walks you into it if you let him.
Win and that belt comes off the plinth for the first time in forty-one years. Lose and you get up, which is still the only rule in here.

topics.label: Tell me about the survey.
replies: Here. Take it — the whole ledger, not a copy.
Four surveys. Every one of them stopped in the same place, four hundred paces past the mouth, at the first bend.
The last one had two foxes in it. Orn came out. Kelm did not, and neither did the bike he took down to save an hour.
What is in that book is torch lines and depths and my handwriting getting worse. What is NOT in it is the chamber past the lake, because nobody has ever reached the chamber past the lake.
Go and reach it.

topics.label: Why fund it yourself?
replies: Because a belt is worth a purse and a purse is worth about four days of a survey, and nobody else was going to.
The pit pays me to be watched. I am using it to look at something instead.

topics.label: What is down in the volcano cave?
replies: Heat, and something that was walking around in it long before we put torches down there.
I go back every season. One of these seasons I will bring an answer out with me.

topics.label: How do I hold a pit?
replies: You do not. You hold it today, and today is all a belt has ever meant.
Anyone who tells you different is selling seats.

topics.label: Champion.
replies: Today. Go on.

topics.label: The Cinder Cup. Give it back.
replies: Ha. They sent YOU. Of course they sent you.
It is behind me on the east wall and it has been polished, which I want you to tell them.
Take it. And tell Lucius that the next time her lot want it back they can come and ask like she just did — through somebody with the sense to wear both colours.
That is twice now this has ended with a conversation. I could get used to that.

npcs.bio: Hero of Luxor and champion of the Fighting Pit. Wears the family gold on her coat and the family scar over her eye, and has never once used either to get out of a bout. Runs the Pit as a boxing hall that happens to be lawless rather than a lawless place that happens to box.

npcs.name: Tace

topics.label: Put me on the card.
replies: Right. Name, and where you have fought.
Volcano Plains. Alone. Yes, I heard, it is why I have not laughed at you.
You are on. Ferro takes the sand himself when there is a new name — that is not a courtesy, it is how he keeps the card worth watching.
Gate is east. Go and be worth the ink.

topics.label: What does a place on the card cost?
replies: Nothing I can take off you. That is the trouble with it.
The pit does not sell places. It gives them to people the crowd would be annoyed not to see, and there is no way to buy that.

topics.label: Who is Ferro, really?
replies: The best fighter on this planet who is still willing to be seen losing.
That is rarer than the other thing. Champions get careful. Ferro never has.

topics.label: Anything worth watching lately?
replies: The pit? No. The plains, though — everyone is talking about the plains.
A thing came up out of the west flat and something put it back down. I have written four different names into the ledger for that and I do not believe any of them.

topics.label: Nothing today.
replies: Then get out of my booth, the queue is imaginary but it is long.

topics.label: How do I get into the Pit?
replies: Same way everyone does. Take the three on the open card — Podd, Vek, Sura, stood along the near side of the ring where you cannot miss them.
Nobody will stop you trying. Nobody will help you either. That is not cruelty, it is the entire point of an open card.

npcs.bio: Keeps the card at the booth. Writes every name down and has never once been asked to prove she did.

npcs.name: Hessa

topics.label: Why not go out and get them?
replies: Because of the bridges. There are three, and something has been coming across them the wrong way.
I have been keeping animals for nineteen years. I know what a spooked herd looks like. This is not spooked. This is EMPTIED — everything on the west side has moved east and it has not moved back.
Make the road safe and I will walk it myself. I am not asking you to catch anything. I am asking you to make it possible for me to.

topics.label: What lives out there?
replies: Lion, wolf, boar, ram, stag, panther, croc down by the water. Ape and serpent if you go far enough west, which nobody does.
Every one of them knew that road before we put a road on it.

topics.label: The plains are clear.
replies: I know. A wolf came down to the feed cart last night and stood there like it was owed something.
Tell the Marshal. He will want it from someone who was out there, not from me telling him what my animals did.

topics.label: Mind how you go.
replies: I always do. It is the whole job.

topics.label: Where does the law stop?
replies: Here. Right where you are standing.
Step past me and whatever you were carrying comes back to your hand on its own. Step back in and it goes away again. You will feel it happen.
Foxes ask me why the King does not just trust everybody. Foxes who ask me that have never seen a market square with thirty people in it.

npcs.bio: Keeps the road menagerie. Ten cages, and she can tell you exactly which four have anything in them without turning round.

npcs.name: Orn

topics.label: What is down there?
replies: Rock that is still moving. A river of it across the passage, one bridge over that, then a hall, then a lake with a span across it and nothing either side of the span but the lake.
And past the span, the chamber. We never reached the chamber. The thing we DID reach was standing in the first bend, four hundred paces in, and it was not one of the brutes off the plains.
It was older. It stood there like it had been standing there.
Take the bridge slow and do not stop on the span. That is all the advice a live surveyor can give you.

topics.label: Who was he?
replies: Kelm. He rode the track before the track had rules. He is the reason there are rules.
He took the bike down because he said walking it would take a day and riding it would take an hour. He was right about the hour.

topics.label: Why not go back in?
replies: Because I would not come out, and then Lyra would come in after me, and then the survey is three foxes instead of one.
I am not brave. I am just still here, which is a different thing and I have had a season to learn the difference.

topics.label: I will come back.
replies: I will be here. That is the one thing I am reliably good at.

npcs.bio: Lyra’s surveyor. Went into the cave with two torches and came out with one, and has been standing at the mouth of it ever since.

npcs.name: Dabb

topics.label: Why does the floor run south?
replies: Because the whole town does. Luxor is built on the skirt of a volcano and the volcano is not finished.
Ask anybody who has laid a floor here. They will tell you a level is a piece of optimism.

topics.label: About the floor.
replies: We are not discussing the floor.
The floor and I have come to an arrangement. It stays where it is and I stop mentioning it.

topics.label: How do I not lose at this?
replies: Stop trying to sink it and start deciding where the white finishes.
That is the whole of it and I have never once managed it. Every shot I take, I hit like I am angry with it.

topics.label: What do people say about the cave?
replies: That there is something in it. That is not a rumour, that is just true, everybody who goes in comes back and says so.
The rumour is the rest of it. That it was down there before us. That it is what the mountain is actually FOR.
I do not believe a word of it and I would not go down there for money.

topics.label: Anything I should know about the plains?
replies: Red plains or volcano plains? Because they are different and the difference will kill you.
Volcano plains is brutes. Slow, heavy, swing once. Red plains is worse lately and nobody will say why, which is how you know it is worse.

topics.label: Who took the crystal?
replies: Ask me on a different night and you will get a different answer, and I will mean both of them.

The bikers say a boxer walked it out. The boxers say a biker rode it out. And a trader in from the red plains says he saw the air bend, out past the river, like heat off a stone with no fire under it.
That last one is nonsense, obviously. He was on his fourth.

topics.label: The trophies.
replies: Cinder Cup at the shop, Iron Belt at the pit, and both of them have slept in the wrong building at least twice.
It is a game. It has always been a game. The day it stops being a game is the day one of them brings something to it that is not a fist, and neither of them ever has.

npcs.bio: Owns the pool table in the sense that nobody has ever managed to get on it while he is in the building.

npcs.name: Sergeant Nix

topics.label: What does a patrol actually find?
replies: Nothing, four times a week, which is the point of doing it four times a week.
You are not looking for a thing. You are looking for the SHAPE of the road, and then one day the shape is wrong and you already know it is wrong before you can say what changed.

topics.label: What changed?
replies: Ground. West of the river the cinder is turned over — not scuffed, TURNED, like something came up through it.
I put that in the book in the spring. I have put it in eleven times since.

topics.label: The Marshal takes bouts?
replies: He takes bouts off anyone who asks and he has never once said no, which tells you what he thinks of most of the asking.
He will not go easy. Do not thank him for that afterwards, he finds it insulting.

topics.label: Carry on, Sergeant.
replies: I was going to.

topics.label: What does the gate check turn up?
replies: Blades, mostly. Honest ones — carters who forgot, hunters coming off the plains with a skinning knife still on the belt.
Never a gang fox. Not once, in two years. They walk through that gate clean every single time, both lots, and they want you to see them do it.
That is not obedience. That is a message.

npcs.bio: Walks the red plains road four times a week and writes down what is not where it was. Nobody reads it. She writes it anyway.

npcs.name: Vail

topics.label: Has the ditch ever been used?
replies: Once, before my time. They filled it and lit it and the story gets better every year it is told.
Mostly it stops carts. A castle that has to be defended has already lost the interesting part of the argument.

topics.label: Anything come up this road lately?
replies: Foxes off the plains with the same face on. Not frightened — ANNOYED, like the road has stopped being theirs.
I log them. Nobody reads it. Nix says the same about her book.

topics.label: Carry on.
replies: I will be here. That is rather the point of a post.

topics.label: Who races this road?
replies: The Run, when the light goes. Torches on the barriers and half the town on the verges.
It is not legal. It is not illegal either, because nobody has ever written it down, and the marshal has decided that not writing it down is a form of policing.

npcs.bio: Stands the north post at the bridge. Has stood it for six years and can tell you the exact day the ditch was last useful.

npcs.name: Ferro

topics.label: How do I fight in here?
replies: Same as anywhere, except the floor is swept and there is nothing to hide behind, so every mistake is one you chose.
Make me miss. A brute swings once and means it; so do I. Anything that swings once has given you the fight the moment it misses.

topics.label: About Lyra.
replies: Three belts and she has never once fought like someone protecting one.
Every purse she has taken has gone straight down that hole in the volcano and nobody in this town will say it out loud but we all know it.

npcs.bio: Luxor’s duellist. Fights left-handed, drinks right-handed, and has never explained which one is the lie.

npcs.name: Patch

topics.label: Who is that at the pool table?
replies: Dabb. Do not play him for money.
Not because he is good. Because he will talk you through every shot he misses and there are a lot of them.

topics.label: Mind how you go.
replies: I will be here.

topics.label: Does the law hold in here?
replies: Better than out there. In here they have to sit down.
Pit on that side, Run on that side, and a strip of floor between them that has been swept more than the rest of the room put together.

npcs.bio: Comes in for one and stays for the argument. Has never bought the second one himself.

npcs.name: Mell

topics.label: The lava jump.
replies: Take it wide and late. Everybody takes it early because it looks shorter and everybody who takes it early lands in the ditch.

topics.label: Enjoy your evening.
replies: I intend to.

topics.label: Which side does this room take?
replies: The side that pays. Which is the Run on a race weekend and the Pit every other night of the week.

npcs.bio: Rides the volcano track on her day off and talks about it on every other day.

npcs.name: Ruck

topics.label: What is a patrol actually for?
replies: Knowing what normal looks like, so you can tell when it stops.
That is it. That is the job. You cannot put it on a poster.

topics.label: Get some rest.
replies: After this one.

topics.label: What happened to your stall?
replies: Nobody hit me. I want that said, because it matters to them and it has stopped mattering to me.
Thirty foxes came to watch two of them and my stall was between the two of them. That is all it takes. That is why we all wear gloves now.

npcs.bio: Off duty, in the same jacket, at the same table. Sergeant Nix says he is the best walker she has and the worst at admitting it.

npcs.name: Sela

topics.label: Copying what?
replies: Whatever is put in front of me. Duty rosters, stock books, a survey now and then.
I do not read them. That is not modesty, it is a business model.

topics.label: I will leave you to it.
replies: Thank you.

topics.label: Do you go to the fights?
replies: Every card. My brother is on the Run and he comes with me and shouts for the boxers, which he would deny under oath.

npcs.bio: Sits in the west booth with her back to the room and a ledger she closes when anybody comes near.

npcs.name: Boge

topics.label: Best fight you have seen?
replies: Lyra, third season, when she was already carrying a bad hand and did not tell anybody until afterwards.
Six minutes. She never once used the hand. That is the whole sport, that is.

topics.label: Enjoy your drink.
replies: Working on it.

topics.label: Do you miss the blades?
replies: I miss the arguments being over faster.
Truthfully? No. My boy drinks in here now. He did not, before.

npcs.bio: Runs the door at the pit on card nights and drinks in the east booth on every other one.

npcs.name: Tib

topics.label: What is Vesta like?
replies: She takes bets on the pit and she has never once been caught.
I have watched her do it from this stool for six years and I still could not tell you how.

topics.label: Good health.
replies: And yours.

topics.label: What is past the gate?
replies: Teeth. Go and find out, everyone else has.

npcs.bio: On the end stool, where he has been since the shift whistle. Knows the price of everything on the shelf and has bought two of them.

npcs.name: Oddi

topics.label: Does it matter?
replies: It matters to the fox who lands on it.
Ask Ferro. He will tell you it is after, and then Tib will say Ferro is being polite, and then we are off again.

topics.label: I will let you get back to it.
replies: We will still be here.

topics.label: What are the odds on the crystal?
replies: I will not take that bet and neither will anybody else in this room, and you should ask yourself why.
A bet needs two sides who think they might be wrong.

npcs.bio: Two stools down from Tib and losing an argument with him that started in the spring.

npcs.name: Rell

topics.label: What is the open card?
replies: Three fighters, all of them hungry, none of them anybody yet.
Podd first — he is the one trying not to look at you. Then Vek, then Sura. Beat one and the next will take you.
They pay out of the gate money. It is not much. It is more than you have.

topics.label: What happens if I lose?
replies: You get up. That is the rule and it is the only rule.
I have swept blood off this sand and I have never once swept anybody off it. Bouts stop before that. Fights outside do not, which is a difference worth learning in here.

topics.label: Can I fight Ferro?
replies: No. Ferro is not open, Ferro is the card.
Tace keeps the card, and the booth is back up the road. She will want to know where you have fought — so go and fight somewhere.

topics.label: Ferro is down here now.
replies: He came down before Tace finished writing you up. That is not eagerness, that is habit.
Take the barrier side. He walks you into it if you let him.

topics.label: Nothing today.
replies: Then stand back off the sand, I have a card to run.

npcs.bio: Runs the open card. Sweeps the sand between bouts and has never once been seen watching one.

npcs.name: Podd

topics.label: Why do this?
replies: Because the alternative is the ash line, and my brother went to the ash line.
Everyone in that seating has a job. I would like one where they say my name while I am doing it.

npcs.bio: Nineteen, and has told everybody in the concourse that he is twenty-two. Wraps his own hands. Badly.

npcs.name: Vek

topics.label: One plan?
replies: Get close. Swing once. It has worked for eleven years and basalt does not dodge.
You will be told I am slow. I am. Being told is not the same as getting out of the way.

npcs.bio: Hauled basalt for eleven years and hits like the eleven years. Has one plan and has never needed a second.

npcs.name: Sura

topics.label: Why not the real card?
replies: Because the real card is one fox deep and he is not going anywhere.
So I hold the top of this one, and every season somebody new comes through and finds out what fast is. It pays. It is not the same as being on the card.

npcs.bio: Quick, awkward, and entirely uninterested in the part of a fight where two foxes agree to stand still.

npcs.name: Holt

topics.label: Say that about wind again.
replies: Everything costs it. Throwing costs it. Holding costs it. MISSING costs half again, which is why the ones who swing at nothing lose to the ones who wait.
A slip you got RIGHT costs almost nothing — that is the reward for watching. A slip you got wrong costs the lot.
Run it to nothing and your guard will not hold, your punches land for a fifth, and everything they throw hits a fox who cannot take it.

topics.label: Slip or guard?
replies: Guard is the safe one. A fifth gets through, it costs you wind, and if you get your hands up in the last moment of his draw-back it is CLEAN — nothing through and he is open.
Slipping is the greedy one. Nothing gets through at all, he is open twice as long, and you finish it more loaded than you started. But you have to be right about which side.
Guard when you do not know. Slip when you do.

topics.label: How do I get the big one off?
replies: You do not throw anything for a second and a half, which means standing in front of a fox who is trying to hit you and doing nothing about it. That is the price and there is no other way to pay it.
So you buy the time. Slip one and he is open long enough to finish loading and put it straight through the middle of him. That is the whole fight, and everything else is arithmetic.
And a punch that lands on you takes most of the wind-up with it. Do not stand there wearing them while it fills.

topics.label: Who is on the card?
replies: Podd drops his left. Every time. He knows and he still does it.
Vek has one punch and you can read it from the road. Do not trade with him, he will take a third of you off. Block it and he is stood there for half a second doing nothing.
Sura will not be where you punch. She is not beating you, she is making you miss until you have nothing left.

topics.label: Does being tougher help in there?
replies: No. Everybody in that ring is the same weight and takes the same punch, and that is the point of a ring.
Whatever you have been doing out on the plains stays out on the plains. In here it is your hands and your wind and whether you were watching.

topics.label: Eight belts.
replies: Somebody won them.
Not all of them me. Not none of them me either. Go and hit the bag.

topics.label: Nothing today.
replies: Then shut the door on your way out, it swings.

npcs.bio: Ringside, always. Eight belts on the board behind Bruno’s counter and he will not say which ones are his.

npcs.name: Wren

topics.label: Why not the card?
replies: Because on the bag I have never lost.
Ask me again when you have been down. I want to know what somebody says about it afterwards.

topics.label: Any advice?
replies: Do not hold your hands up the whole time. I did that for a year. You cannot hit anybody from behind your own gloves, you run out of wind doing nothing, and the meter just sits there.
Up when it is coming, down the rest of the time. That is the only thing I know that Holt did not tell me.

topics.label: Nothing today.
replies: Right. Bag is free.

npcs.bio: Six rounds on the bag every morning and has never once been on the card. Says she is not ready. Holt disagrees.

npcs.name: Vash

lines.text: NO WEAPONS in town. Been too many gang fights so now BOXING GLOVES ONLY.
WHAT IF I need my weapons?
YOU can equip weapons outside of town. BEHAVE yourself and the GLOVES are yours to keep.

npcs.bio: City guard. Draws the short straw on pad duty and has made peace with it.

npcs.name: Lucius

topics.label: Take me to the line.
replies: You have been in here twice and looked at the rack both times.
The mountain, then. Three circuits on it and the first one is free, which is a thing I only say to foxes with no colours on.
FOLLOW ME.

topics.label: Who has your trophy?
replies: The Pit has it. Off the plinth, out the door, and not one of us laid a hand on them because that is not how this is done.
It will be at the pit, on the east side, next to their own. They like them side by side. They think it is funny.
Go and ask for it. You are one of ours and one of theirs, which makes you the only fox on this planet who can.

npcs.bio: Hero of Luxor and the fox behind the counter at the Bike Shop. The only one of the three who reads the ledger, which is why the Run has a route through the Red Plains and the Pit has a card. Wears the coat cut narrow and the crest without the gold.

npcs.name: Cobb
npcs.bio: Lives on the tune pad. Has never finished a sentence without looking at a wheel.

npcs.name: Jax

topics.label: I am going into the volcano.
replies: Then you are going in with more than your hands, or you are not coming out of it.
Scattergun. Seven in a cone, no reach at all — which is the right weapon in a tunnel and the wrong one everywhere else.
It stays holstered until you are past the last gate. Law is the law and I am not carrying your fine.
Come out of that mountain and it is yours. Do not come out and it was never mine either.

npcs.bio: Outside the shop, every day, watching the road. Somebody has to.

npcs.name: Tarn
npcs.bio: Marshals the circuit and the ash, and prefers the ash.

npcs.name: Brek

topics.label: How does a fox get on the card?
replies: Tace keeps it. Booth on Pit Road, east out of the square.
Three names on the open card and they stand in a line in front of the ring so you cannot pretend you did not see them. Podd, Vek, Sura.
Take all three and Lyra will call you one of us. Take one and you will have learned something, which is not nothing.

npcs.bio: Stands outside the gym in his wraps. Has never once been asked to and has never once not been there.

npcs.name: Hest

lines.text: Lox is on the seat. Do not lean on the rail.

npcs.bio: Left of the steps, every day of his life so far.

npcs.name: Mord

lines.text: Lox is on the seat. Do not lean on the rail.

npcs.bio: Right of the steps. Has never had to draw anything in this room.

npcs.name: Yuki
npcs.bio: An Earth fox — a kitsune — and the only one on this planet who is not from one of the ten worlds. Sent to find the foxes who left Earth and tell them what has been happening to the crystals since they did. Lost in space for years before she found the first fox world; taken within the hour of saying so out loud.

npcs.name: Yuki
npcs.bio: An Earth fox — a kitsune — and the only one on this planet who is not from one of the ten worlds. Sent to find the foxes who left Earth and tell them what has been happening to the crystals since they did. Lost in space for years before she found the first fox world; taken within the hour of saying so out loud.

npcs.name: Fenn

topics.label: Two out of nine?
replies: He is longer than me and he knows exactly how much longer. Every time I come in he has already decided where I am going to be.
The trick is not being faster. The trick is arriving somewhere he has not already measured. I have not found one yet.

npcs.bio: In the cage since the second bell, and losing. Cheerful about it, which Sark finds worse than the losing.

npcs.name: Sark

topics.label: Does he ever get close?
replies: Twice. Both times because he did something that made no sense, and the thing about a reach advantage is it only works on foxes who make sense.
I have started watching for it. Which means he has already cost me something.

npcs.bio: Longer in the arm than anyone in the building and entirely aware of it. Has won seven and mentioned all seven.

npcs.name: Wick
npcs.bio: Leans on the cage rail scoring bouts nobody asked him to score. Keeps the tally in his head and it is always right.

npcs.name: Bray
npcs.bio: Off the night watch, eating at a table built for sixteen with nobody at the other fifteen places.

npcs.name: Cass
npcs.bio: On the vault door. Has been on the vault door long enough that the Marshal has stopped putting anyone else on it.

npcs.name: Pell
npcs.bio: Off duty at the bunk wing, boots off, not asleep and not pretending to be.

npcs.name: Nore
npcs.bio: Reading the back of a bottle at the potion stack with the expression of somebody who has read it before.

npcs.name: Fig
npcs.bio: At the gear shelves, holding two of the same thing and looking from one to the other.

npcs.name: Quill
npcs.bio: At the display table by the door, where the things nobody needs are put where everybody has to walk past them.

npcs.name: Dace
npcs.bio: Waiting at the grindstone with something wrapped in cloth and no intention of unwrapping it until Garrow is free.

npcs.name: Bryn

topics.label: Why look if you will not buy?
replies: Because everything in here has been in the fire twice and you can see which twice.
The second time is what you are paying for. Anybody can heat a thing once.

npcs.bio: At the blade rack, not buying. Comes in to look, which Garrow has decided to be flattered by.

npcs.name: Halla
npcs.bio: Garrison, off duty, standing in front of an armour stand doing sums she does not like the answer to.

npcs.name: Gid

topics.label: Why threes?
replies: Because the third one is the one they have stopped expecting. The first two are just buying it.
Holt taught me that and then spent a season telling me I throw the first two too well. They are meant to be cheap.

npcs.bio: On the end bag, working it in threes and counting out loud without noticing he is doing it.

npcs.name: Mox
npcs.bio: Under the squat rack, on the last set, at the point in it where talking is not free.

npcs.name: Gault

topics.label: Why hold a road to nowhere?
replies: Because it is the only one. One mouth in, the same mouth out. Whatever is in there has to come through us to get to the zoo path, and the zoo path goes to the square.
Two of us is not enough to stop it. Two of us is enough to be the ones who say it is coming.

npcs.bio: At the mouth of the camp with his back to the road, which is the direction he is paid to have his back to.

npcs.name: Bel
npcs.bio: Keeps the camp fire and the tally of what has walked past it. The tally is longer than the fire has been lit.

npcs.name: Pia
npcs.bio: Runs the counter. Has never once been seen to hurry and has never once been behind.

npcs.name: Lucius

lines.text: "You are on the line. That is further than most of them get."

topics.label: What am I riding?
replies: The blue one off the rack, and it is not a loan.
Four gears, one burner, and a heat gauge that will boil you if you hold it like a button. Hold it like a decision.

topics.label: Which way round?
replies: Follow the arrows. They have pointed that way since before I was riding it.
And when you have had enough of circuits, keep following them. They end up somewhere.

npcs.bio: Hero of Luxor and the fox behind the counter at the Bike Shop. The only one of the three who reads the ledger, which is why the Run has a route through the Red Plains and the Pit has a card. Wears the coat cut narrow and the crest without the gold.

npcs.name: Cinder

lines.text: Hot today.
It is hot every day. You are asking about the wind.

npcs.bio: Sweeps ash off the crossing every morning and again every afternoon.

npcs.name: Rill

lines.text: What is south?
The volcano. Walk the plains if you like, but not the cave. Not alone.

npcs.bio: Rides the volcano track on rest days and has the scars to show for it.

npcs.name: Tam

lines.text: Anything on tonight?
Pit, west road. There is always something on at the pit.

npcs.bio: Sells cold water at the pit gate and makes a year's living in a season.

npcs.name: Odile

lines.text: Hello.
New face. Buy boots with a thick sole; the ground here takes them off you.

npcs.bio: Cornered for Bruno once. Talks about it more than Bruno does.

npcs.name: Beck

lines.text: Who runs Luxor?
The castle. And Bruno, in the gym, in every way that matters to me.

npcs.bio: Keeps the square's lamps lit. Knows which ones the heat keeps breaking.

npcs.name: Sorrel

lines.text: Quiet street.
Everyone is at the pit or asleep. There is no third thing.

npcs.bio: Was born on the red plains and moved to town for the shade.

lines.text: Welcome to Luxor, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.
